title: Classify cyclic periods of balanced depth-three chain schedules (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Balanced correct-word counts cannot always be divided by the word length to count cyclic schedules. This package proves the exact repetition and rotation-period law for the unsigned depth-three dirty chain, for every modulus. At `(m,c)=(3,1)`, the known 24 length-nine words form **four** cyclic classes: two of size nine and two of size three.

For a unit target, every nonprimitive balanced correct word repeats exactly three times. Such words exist precisely when `m=3n`, `3∤n`, and `c≡n³ (mod 3)`, except at **(6,5) and (12,1)**. The sufficiency direction uses the credited predecessor balanced-existence theorem. General fixed-point and Möbius formulas give every least-period population and the exact cyclic count from `W(m,c)`.

Only `research/chain-cyclic-schedules/` is added. This is a **scoped proof with finite exact corroboration**, with no new κ, supplier, paid-profile change or measured speedup. Rotation equivalence concerns the universal endpoint; routing, precision and word-dependent physical costs remain separate. This does not prove #6037's all-modulus distinctness conjecture or a closed formula for W.

[Proof and boundaries](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a2d0504b3937c9513dc13787cfee56a4f983ef1f/research/chain-cyclic-schedules/PROOF.md)

## Task and overlap

Canonical base: `721c03822c421b7f7fcbb2598993b947c4d88419`, priority revision 8. The original `connector-alphabet-change` card is retained verbatim, with **scope_status=changed** to a counting side question in the unchanged alphabet. The result supplies exact rotational deduplication and divisibility checks; it does not supply a favorable completed budget.

Nearest work: Nick Petalas's [#6037](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6037) counts literal words; [#4257](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4257) classifies depth-three profiles and tariffs; [#4281](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4281) already observes rotation closure; [#4748](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4748) classifies one binary depth-six rotation class. The all-modulus depth-three stabilizer law and unit-target existence classification are the addition here.

Original #6037 head: `88331a098ad9f0299e205bb103acc55b2dc087df`. Consumed bytes are retained unchanged in publication ancestor `ccff0fb7ed8f53a686a3f2ecc2a5585d7bd8a505`; source pins resolve to that ancestor, with original path/head/blob and credit preserved separately. Cold reproduction does not require the pending predecessor's cached Git object.

The final overlap report covers 341 open PRs, 5,722 Discussion records and 5,222 closed/merged PRs at the recorded timestamps. The closed refresh timed out; a subsequent updated-order API check found no closed PR updates after the retained cutoff. Latest open submissions through #6072 were checked separately. These metadata searches are not a novelty certificate or a search of all historical diffs.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.10, Windows 11 x64, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/chain-cyclic-schedules
```

- Exhausted **793,182** balanced words for m=1..5, including the formal modulus-one convention. Independent literal fixed points, least periods and canonical rotations agree.
- Checked **536,472** full-matrix rotations and **291,408** repeated-block identities; independently reproduced W by chronological DP through m=8.
- All **179** unit-target cases through m=24 satisfy the new classification. Rows above m=8 are **derived from frozen #6037 counts**, not a new independent high-modulus census.
- Normal and optimized full receipts match; 13 explicit false-claim controls pass. Eleven actual private-copy mutations are rejected in both modes (**22 rejections**), with two passing unchanged probes.
- Committed-byte and official export checks pass. The exact scientific snapshot was replayed without Git from read-only exported files: normal, optimized and mutation checks all pass, with no exported file changes. This also verifies the repaired Windows temporary-copy permission handling.

The unchanged canonical base still fails two current-status documentation tests; the separate [#6050](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6050) addresses them. These are distinguished from the passing package checks. On the submitted head `abdcee87d8eb0f46db522b16596406f43e890d7e`, [hosted run 40636404155](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40636404155/job/122644265680) ran 678 helper tests and ended with exactly those two failures (23 skipped); the scientific replay job was consequently skipped. This is a shared-plan failure, not a remote failure of the new mathematical checks. Full selected-supplier cold replay, full-history preflight in this shallow checkout, proof-kernel verification and independent human review are not claimed. The validation note records the precise limits.

## Credit

Nick Petalas retains credit for the counts, interval reduction, balanced-existence theorem and rotation precedents; Ross Richardson's #943/#934 lineage supplies the complete-call dirty-connector interface. Burnside's lemma and Möbius inversion are classical. Source notices and Apache-2.0 are retained.

Prepared for **SHIN09-git with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance** in proof, implementation and writing. Both implementations have the same assisted author; no global literature-priority claim.

## Open next questions

Can a representative generator attain the cyclic quotient with a fully counted runtime improvement? The smallest useful test is the 356 classes at (5,1). Separately, derive all depth-four repetition constraints before attempting a higher-depth quotient. Neither follow-up is claimed complete here.
